subject: Routing tie-breaks and per-route breakdowns for Console: ask + exceptions
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Routing tie-breaks + per-route breakdown ask for Console

Hi Marcus / Kim (cc Jonas),

Quick ask as we prep the next Console sprint: Acme's SRE flagged a gap where our Console shows aggregate cost by endpoint, but not callchain-level splits when a request touches multiple routes (example: web -> reranker -> generator). They want to be able to: 

- See per-route token/latency costs for an end-to-end request ID
- Filter by priority lane (realtime vs batch) and see tie-breaks when routing falls back to cheaper model variants
- Surface the top-3 contributing routes to cost and the last-successful-fallback used when SLA was met

Example: I attached a small export from their tenant (per-route-sample.csv) to illustrate the current confusion.

Can we get a short feasibility summary from Product/Infra/Analytics by EOD Monday? Specifically:
1) Marcus: cost attribution model — can we attribute tokens/compute to routes within a single request id without a heavy re-ingest?
2) Kim: UI surface — a compact per-request drilldown (3 columns: route, token_count, p95 latency) vs a new callchain view — what do you think is lower friction?
3) Jonas: sampling/backfill — can we produce a 7-day stitched view for Acme for their audit?

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Tue AM to align scope and fast-fail if it's infra-prohibitive.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: per-route-sample.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Sep 2028 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing tie-breaks + per-route breakdown ask for Console

Thanks Neha — good example. Quick notes after a run-through with infra: 

- Short answer: doable, with two caveats.
  1) If we rely solely on current ingest (per-request logs + path metadata) we can produce a conservative attribution by splitting tokens/latency proportionally by measured per-hop durations. That avoids reprocessing model traces but is approximate.
  2) For precise attribution (e.g., token-level accounting per model shard/variant) we need KV-cache hooks or an additional small envelope emitted by the serving runtime per token-range — that requires a small runtime change and a rollout window (~3 sprints).

- Cost: proportional splitting is cheap and can be done in the Console backend as a transformation job; precise accounting introduces an extra 0.5-1% runtime overhead on hot paths and needs a feature flag.

I'll scope two proposals: Quick (approximate) and Precise (runtime + backend). Will post PRD by Monday noon.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Samantha <samantha@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Sep 2028 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing tie-breaks + per-route breakdown ask for Console

Hi all — attaching a mock (console-mockups-v2.png) that tests two UX patterns: 

A) Inline per-request callchain (compact): expands a request id to show each route row with token/latency/cost columns. Pros: minimal navigation, fast for auditors. Cons: can get wide for long chains.

B) Callchain graph view: visual waterfall with top contributors highlighted and a right rail showing last fallback details. Pros: clearer contribution ordering; Cons: needs more engineering for interactive zoom.

Recommendation: ship A as an MVP behind a flag; if infra supports precise hooks later, we upgrade to B with traces. 

Samantha — does Acme have a preference? If you can confirm whether auditors prefer CSV exports or interactive UI, that helps prioritize.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Console
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Samantha Rios <samantha@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing tie-breaks + per-route breakdown ask for Console

Thanks — the mock looks great. For Acme's auditors, CSV export is mandatory for quarterly reviews, but an interactive UI is a huge help for day-to-day debugging. Priorities: 

1) CSV export with per-route rows and request id grouping (this is critical).
2) Inline per-request callchain view (pattern A) as MVP.
3) Later: If you can mark the last fallback model and its cost delta, that will resolve most of our billing disputes.

We can do the Tue sync if you confirm time; otherwise, send the PRD and we can comment in-line.

—Sam
Samantha Rios
SRE Lead, Acme Corp
